definitions.explanation: Warm air, especially as a meteorological term referring to a warm air mass or warm front.

definitions.gloss: warming up; idling to warm up (an engine)
definitions.explanation: The act of running an engine at idle to bring it to operating temperature before driving. Also written as 暖機.

examples.japanese: {南|みなみ}から{暖気|だんき}が{流|なが}れ{込|こ}んでいる。
examples.english: Warm air is flowing in from the south.

examples.japanese: {暖気|だんき}と{寒気|かんき}がぶつかると{前線|ぜんせん}ができる。
examples.english: When warm and cold air masses collide, a front forms.

examples.japanese: {週末|しゅうまつ}にかけて{暖気|だんき}が{入|はい}り、{気温|きおん}が{上|あ}がる{見込|みこ}みだ。
examples.english: Warm air is expected to move in toward the weekend, raising temperatures.

examples.japanese: {冬|ふゆ}は{暖気|だんき}{運転|うんてん}をしてから{出発|しゅっぱつ}する。
examples.english: In winter, I warm up the engine before setting off.

examples.japanese: {最近|さいきん}の{車|くるま}は{暖気|だんき}が{必要|ひつよう}ないと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: They say modern cars don't need to be warmed up.

examples.japanese: エンジンの{暖気|だんき}が{終|お}わるまで{少|すこ}し{待|ま}ってください。
examples.english: Please wait a moment until the engine finishes warming up.

notes:
CONTRAST:
{暖気|だんき} (warm air) vs. {寒気|かんき} (cold air) — these are a natural pair in weather reports.

NOTE ON KANJI:
When referring to warming up an engine (sense 2), the word is also written {暖機|だんき} (with the kanji for "machine"). Both spellings are used.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {暖気|だんき}{運転|うんてん} (idling to warm up)
- {暖気|だんき}が{流|なが}れ{込|こ}む (warm air flows in)
